summary: Covington County, AL former lookout built about 1940 on former Conecuh National Forest land; removed after 1977; now privately owned.

facts.design: Believed to have had a 12'x12' cab with catwalk
facts.status_note: Former Fire Lookout Sites lists the tower as removed after 1977; no source describes what remains at the site

access.note: Register lists a private owner after a land swap; no public access described

events.note: Built circa 1940 per the register's Built field
Removed after 1977 per the register's Removed field; 1977 is a lower bound, not the removal year
Registered March 24, 2020; nominated by Al Pelham

evidence.supports: built on former Conecuh National Forest land, now privately owned after a land swap
evidence.quote: It was built on a parcel of land that had been part of the Conecuh National Forest but is now privately owned due to a land swap

evidence.supports: believed 12 by 12 foot cab with catwalk
evidence.quote: This tower is believed to have had a 12'-by-12' cab with catwalk.

evidence.supports: administered by a private owner, formerly the Forest Service
usual explanation: aircraft spot fires over a broader area than a 100-foot tower
evidence.quote: The most common explanation is that aircraft was more efficient in spotting fires in a much broader area than a 100-foot tower could provide

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

corrections.why: The register says 'after 1977', so 1977 is the earliest the removal could be, not the removal year
The register gives the build date as circa 1940, not an exact year

notes_for_editor: The register is the only source for the build date, design, removal, and land swap. The land swap and the 12x12 cab are the register's own wording and are not confirmed elsewhere. A Forest Service 'Land Exchange with Kobal LLC' record for Conecuh NF appeared in search results but was not read and the snippet did not name a tower, so it is not cited. The Open Pond tower (CCC-built 1938-39, NHLR #97, Conecuh NF) is a different tower and was not used. Other towers named Yellow River (Iowa, Florida) are unrelated. Searches used: 2 (one websearch.py fallback, one WebSearch). Page reads: FFLOS page, Conecuh NF Wikipedia (grep), Kaufmann article.
